The degrees of freedom give a cochain isomorphism from
$$W_h^0\xrightarrow{\nabla}N_h^1\xrightarrow{\operatorname{curl}}N_h^2\xrightarrow{\operatorname{div}}N_h^3$$
to $C^0\xrightarrow{\delta^0}C^1\xrightarrow{\delta^1}C^2\xrightarrow{\delta^2}C^3$. Consequently the discrete cohomology in degree $k$ is naturally isomorphic to $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(H_k(|\mathcal T|;\mathbb R),\mathbb R)$. For general topology, define
$$\mathcal H_h^1:=\ker(\operatorname{curl}|_{N_h^1})\cap(\nabla W_h^0)^\perp,\qquad \mathcal H_h^2:=\ker(\operatorname{div}|_{N_h^2})\cap(\operatorname{curl}N_h^1)^\perp$$

These have the same uniform bounds, are the identity on $E_{h,0}^k$, and commute in degrees zero through two on the homogeneous complex; the terminal degree-three differential is zero. In particular,
$$\pi_{h,0}^0:H_0^1(\Omega)\to W_h^0\cap H_0^1(\Omega),\qquad \pi_{h,0}^1:H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)\to N_h^1\cap H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega),\qquad \nabla\pi_{h,0}^0=\pi_{h,0}^1\nabla.$$
Here the zero tangential space uses [[def-na-zero-tangential-hcurl]]. Each family converges strongly in $L^2$ on every $L^2$ form, uniformly on compact $L^2$ subsets, and in the graph norm on its corresponding graph domain. The full and homogeneous families are separate operators. These are cochain projections; canonical edge moments are not asserted bounded on $H(\operatorname{curl})$.

Differentiate e_theta,e_phi: e_theta dot partial_phi e_phi=-cos theta and e_phi dot partial_phi e_theta=cos theta. Therefore v dagger partial_phi v=-i sigma cos theta. planned_items.statement: On oriented affine Minkowski space with eta=diag(-1,1,1,1) and vol=dx0 wedge dx1 wedge dx2 wedge dx3, define star by alpha wedge star beta=<alpha,beta>_eta vol using determinant-normalized exterior pairing. For a smooth closed k-form omega, its period on a smooth compact oriented k-cycle z is integral_z omega. Exactness means omega=d a globally. No physical constants or physical premises enter this definition.

For this signature in dimension four, star squared on k-forms is (-1)^(k(4-k)+1); in particular star squared=-I on two-forms, star(dx0 wedge dx1)=-dx2 wedge dx3, and star(dx2 wedge dx3)=dx0 wedge dx1.

On a star-shaped open U in R4 with centre a every smooth closed two-form F has potential A_mu(x)=integral_0^1 t (x-a)^nu F_{nu mu}(a+t(x-a)) dt. On any smooth manifold a closed F admits a global smooth real one-form potential exactly when [F]=0 in H2_dR; a nonzero period precludes exactness.
On R3 minus the origin, beta=(x dy wedge dz+y dz wedge dx+z dx wedge dy)/(x2+y2+z2)^(3/2) is closed and has period 4 pi on the oriented unit sphere, hence is not globally exact.
On the punctured plane A=(-y dx+x dy)/(x2+y2) is closed, has circle period 2 pi and is not d chi for a globally single-valued real chi; local potentials differ by constants.

In a fixed oriented SI lab chart define E1=E_i dx_i, B2=B1 dy wedge dz+B2 dz wedge dx+B3 dx wedge dy, D2 analogously, H1=H_i dx_i, and J3=rho dx wedge dy wedge dz-dt wedge (J1 dy wedge dz+J2 dz wedge dx+J3 dx wedge dy). Define F=B2-dt wedge E1 and G=D2+dt wedge H1. Here F components in x0=ct are the existing F_0i=-E_i/c. F integrals have Wb, G integrals C, and J3 integrals C; component dimensions depend on dt versus dx0.

For C1 macroscopic fields with conserved sources, dF=0 and dG=J3 are equivalent to the four SI macroscopic Maxwell equations. In vacuum D=epsilon0 E,H=B/mu0 gives G=(mu0 c)^-1 star F. Exterior differentiation implies dJ3=0. On a fixed spatial cycle the magnetic flux period is constant in time when the cycle is transported only by lab time.

On a source-free vacuum region, for constant theta, F_theta=cos(theta)F+sin(theta)star F again solves dF_theta=d star F_theta=0. Generic electric sources, PEC boundaries and material laws break this symmetry; no claim of a magnetic charge sector is adopted.

A source-free exterior region may carry nonzero magnetic two-form periods that prevent a single global potential. Such data require interior/boundary flux specification and are not an inference of magnetic charge in the full-space Maxwell model.
A nonzero tangential magnetic field adjacent to a PEC plane can be mapped by vacuum duality to a nonzero tangential electric field, violating the same PEC boundary condition.

Let Omega be a bounded Lipschitz polyhedron. H(curl) is the L2 distributional-curl graph space; H0(curl) is the closure of compactly supported smooth vectors in this norm. Fields E,H are C1 in time with values in L2 and continuous into H(curl) where Green pairings are used. Real time-independent symmetric epsilon,mu in L-infinity have uniform eigenvalue bounds 0<a<=lambda<=b; D=epsilon E,B=mu H. PEC means E in H0(curl). Smooth impedance data use H_tan=Y(n cross E), Y>=0, with surface power n dot(E cross H)=Y |E_tan|2. Rough impedance is only asserted when these traces and products lie in L2 of the boundary.

Under the preceding boundary model and epsilon E_t=curl H-J, mu H_t=-curl E, energy W=1/2 integral(E dot epsilon E+H dot mu H) obeys Wdot=-integral E dot J for PEC; with admissible impedance add -integral_boundary Y |E_tan|2. Thus zero-data homogeneous solutions are unique. This is an a-priori result for solutions in the specified class, not an existence theorem.

For a fixed oriented C2 interface with n from minus to plus, piecewise C1 fields with joint one-sided spacetime C1 extensions and C1 surface free charge sigma and tangential surface current K, the distributional Maxwell equations imply n dot[D]=sigma,n cross[H]=K,n dot[B]=0,n cross[E]=0 and sigma_t+div_surface K+n dot[J]=0, with no edge of the interface in the test support.

The Coulomb field of a point charge is locally integrable but not locally L2 near its support: integral_{delta<r<R} epsilon0 |E|2/2 diverges proportionally to 1/delta. A distributional Maxwell solution alone therefore does not define a finite stress tensor.
For n=e_z and tangential E=E0 e_x, H=Y(n cross E)=Y E0 e_y gives outward power Y E0 squared, while the reversed sign injects energy.

In the rest frame of a homogeneous nonmagnetic material adopt D=epsilon_infinity E+sum P_l, B=mu H, and P_l,tt+gamma_l P_l,t+omega_l squared P_l=a_l E, for finitely many oscillators with epsilon_infinity,mu,a_l,omega_l>0 and gamma_l>=0. Quantities are real spatial vectors; epsilon_infinity has F/m and mu has H/m; P is C/m2, a_l has units F/(m s2), omega,gamma s^-1. Histories specify P and P_t, with a zero-past branch for the causal convolution. This is a linear local-response model, not a derivation of microscopic matter.

For smooth oscillator-medium solutions the sum of electromagnetic energy with epsilon_infinity and mu and W_l=(|P_l,t|2+omega_l squared |P_l|2)/(2 a_l) obeys partial_t W+div(E cross H)=-Jfree dot E-sum gamma_l |P_l,t|2/a_l. In particular undriven closed PEC systems have nonincreasing positive energy.

With phasors exp(-i omega t) the zero-history electric susceptibility is sum a_l/(omega_l squared-z squared-i gamma_l z), analytic for Im z>0; for real omega>0 away from undamped poles Im epsilon(omega)>=0. For gamma_l>0 every kernel is exponentially decaying, is causal, and supports the usual unsubtracted Hilbert-transform relation for epsilon-epsilon_infinity. Undamped poles require distributional boundary limits; a pointwise dispersion formula there is not asserted.

In the same fixed homogeneous material rest frame adopt a free carrier current V with V_t+gamma V=a E, P_t=V, D=epsilon_infinity E+P, B=mu H, with a,epsilon_infinity,mu>0 and gamma>=0. V is A/m2 and a is F/(m s2). The zero-past current branch is causal; a constant polarization offset is separately specified by Gauss data. This is a phenomenological closure and makes no microscopic carrier-statistics assertion.

For exp(-i omega t), omega>0, the closure has conductivity a/(gamma-i omega), nonnegative Re conductivity, epsilon(omega)=epsilon_infinity-a/[omega(omega+i gamma)], and stored carrier energy |V|2/(2a). Field plus carrier energy loses gamma |V|2/a. In the collisionless branch epsilon=epsilon_infinity-a/omega2 and transverse plane waves have k2=mu epsilon_infinity(omega2-omega_p2), omega_p2=a/epsilon_infinity. Below omega_p they are evanescent rather than real-k propagating bulk modes.

Take epsilon_infinity=epsilon0, mu=mu0, a=epsilon0 omega0 squared and gamma=omega0/2, and put nu=omega/omega0. On the passive square-root branch n=sqrt(1+1/(1-nu squared-i nu/2)), k=(omega/c)n. At nu=1, d Re k/d omega is negative, so a narrow-band group delay can be negative in this lossy causal model; it does not define the support front of a signal.
An undamped oscillator at a time with P=0,P_t nonzero carries strictly positive energy |P_t|2/(2a), so the instantaneous pair E,D cannot determine total stored energy.

For homogeneous lossless epsilon=epsilon transpose>0 and mu scalar>0 in a fixed material frame, monochromatic E=Re(e exp(i k dot x-i omega t)), omega>0, has b=k cross e/omega and equation k cross(mu^-1 k cross e)+omega squared epsilon e=0, with k dot epsilon e=0. E need not be orthogonal to k; D is. The symbols k,omega have units m^-1,s^-1.

For epsilon=diag(epsilon_perp,epsilon_perp,epsilon_parallel)>0, k=(kx,0,kz), the ordinary branch has kx squared+kz squared=mu epsilon_perp omega squared; the extraordinary branch has kx squared/epsilon_parallel+kz squared/epsilon_perp=mu omega squared. No complex conjugation occurs in this bilinear reciprocity identity.
For kx kz nonzero and epsilon_perp not equal epsilon_parallel, an extraordinary polarization may satisfy k dot D=0 while k dot E is nonzero.
A scalar complex epsilon with positive imaginary part and real positive mu satisfies the reciprocity hypothesis yet absorbs cycle-averaged electric power omega Im(epsilon)|E|2/2.

Let smooth conserved rho,J have support in one ball B_a for all relevant times and all derivatives needed on a bounded retarded-time interval be bounded. Put t=u+r/c, x=r n. For those sources and r>=2a, define Q(n,u)=integral J(y,u+n dot y/c)dy. Then E=-(mu0/(4 pi r))(I-n n transpose) partial_u Q+O(r^-2), B=n cross E/c+O(r^-2), uniformly in n and u on compact intervals, with constants controlled by support radius and finite uniform source derivative bounds. Hence radiated power at u is (mu0/(16 pi squared c)) integral_S2 |n cross partial_u Q|2 dOmega.

Assume additionally a bound on partial_t squared J. Then |partial_u Q(n,u)-integral partial_t J(y,u)dy| <= (a/c) integral sup_{|s-u|<=a/c}|partial_t squared J(y,s)|dy. The leading electric dipole power is |p_tt|2/(6 pi epsilon0 c3); the displayed amplitude bound yields an absolute power error by |v2-w2|<=|v-w|(2|w|+|v-w|), not a relative error at a dipole zero.
For dipole acceleration p_tt parallel to n, the leading radiation amplitude vanishes although higher multipoles need not; a uniform absolute error does not imply a uniform relative error.
For a compact pulse, taking r to infinity with t fixed samples the pre-pulse field and may give zero, while t=u+r/c keeps its radiative pulse visible.

For a prescribed smooth external force f(t), mass m>0, and tau=q2/(6 pi epsilon0 m c3)>0, adopt m(a-tau a_t)=f as an effective nonrelativistic point-particle equation. This is an additional restricted model and not a well-defined substitution of the singular Maxwell self-field in the Lorentz force. a has units m/s2 and tau seconds.

For the Abraham–Lorentz equation all solutions differ by C exp(t/tau). If f is bounded continuous and the exponentially weighted future integral converges, the unique bounded-future acceleration is a(t)=(m tau)^-1 integral_t^infinity exp(-(s-t)/tau) f(s)ds. It can be nonzero before a nonzero future force starts.

For f in C2, a_RO=(f+tau f_t)/m has residual m(a_RO-tau a_RO,t)-f=-tau2 f_tt. If f_tt is uniformly bounded and the bounded-future branch is chosen, its difference from a_RO is at most tau2 sup|f_tt|/m. These estimates concern prescribed-force acceleration, not an uncontrolled nonlinear self-consistent trajectory.
f=0 admits a=C exp(t/tau), so the equation plus position and velocity at one instant alone fails to select a physical branch.
For f=Re(f0 exp(-i omega t)) the exact nonrunaway acceleration amplitude is f0/[m(1+i omega tau)] and reduction of order is accurate only when |omega tau| is small in the absolute error bound.

Let a:R3 minus {0} to C3 be smooth with compact support away from k=0 and k dot a=0. Define A_plus(x,t)=(2 pi)^(-3/2) integral a(k) exp(i k dot x-i c|k|t)dk, real A=2 Re A_plus, E=-A_t,B=curl A. On the transverse fibre at k nonzero let C(k)v=i khat cross v. Then C is Hermitian, C squared=P_T=I-khat khat transpose, and P_plus/minus=(P_T plus/minus C)/2 are orthogonal rank-one projectors whose sum is P_T. Their Fourier multipliers commute with vacuum time evolution and proper spatial rotations. A global smooth nonvanishing polarization basis is not assumed.

For these real Schwartz vacuum fields define Jkin=epsilon0 integral x cross(E cross B)dx, Lcan=epsilon0 sum_i integral E_i (x cross grad)A_i dx, and Scan=epsilon0 integral E cross A dx. All carry J s. These are functionals on the specified gauge-fixed fields, not separately universal local gauge-invariant densities.

For the stated Schwartz Coulomb-gauge vacuum fields Jkin=Lcan+Scan. The identity relies on div E=0 and vanishing surface terms; with charge density the integral decomposition includes epsilon0 integral (div E)(x cross A)dx, and finite boundaries also contribute a surface term.

A nonzero monochromatic plane wave fills infinite space with positive mean energy density and is outside the finite-energy functionals; the finite-energy total-angular-momentum functional is therefore outside its defined domain; formal component cancellations do not change that fact.

For a smooth charge-supported configuration and decaying potentials the algebraic split includes integral rho x cross A, so dropping div E is valid only in the source-free region with the specified boundaries.

Fix vacuum k0=omega/c>0 and 0<delta<1. Let uhat in L2(R2) be supported in |q|<=delta k0. Define u_exact(z)=Fourier_inverse[exp(i z sqrt(k0 squared-|q|2)) uhat(q)] and u_par(z)=exp(i k0 z) Fourier_inverse[exp(-i z |q|2/(2k0)) uhat(q)]. These are scalar envelopes, with Fourier inverse normalized unitarily. An exact vector spectrum e(q) must satisfy (q,kz) dot e=0.

For real z the L2 envelope error is at most |z| k0 delta4/[8(1-delta2)^(3/2)] times ||u0||2. For an exact vector wave its longitudinal spectrum satisfies |e_z|<=delta/sqrt(1-delta2)|e_perp|. Thus a small angular cone alone does not give a uniformly small long-distance phase error.

For a smooth paraxial scalar envelope u(r,phi,z)=f(r,z) exp(i ell phi), integer ell, with finite transverse norm and vanishing radial boundary terms, -i partial_phi u=ell u. The normalized scalar angular-generator expectation is ell; identifying a torque or a photon angular momentum requires additional vector flux or QFT assumptions.
For spectra concentrated near |q|=delta k0 and propagation z proportional to (k0 delta4)^-1, the difference between exact and paraxial phase need not tend to zero as delta tends to zero.
For q nonzero, prescribing e_perp parallel to q gives nonzero e_z, so a scalar transverse polarization prescription alone is not an exact Maxwell beam.

Let Me in R^(ne x ne), Mb in R^(nb x nb) be symmetric positive definite, C in R^(nb x ne), S positive semidefinite, and D in R^(nc x nb) satisfy D C=0. Define W=1/2(e transpose Me e+b transpose Mb b), algebraic weak-divergence constraint q=-G transpose Me e for any G with C G=0, and magnetic constraint D b. For continuous j and initial e,b the finite system has a unique C1 solution on every finite interval, W_t=-e transpose S e-e transpose j, D b(t)=D b(0), and q_t=G transpose(S e+j).

Inputs are the preceding matrices with S=0,j=0, time step h>0, integer N>=0, e0 and b_minus_half. For n=0,...,N-1 set b_{n+1/2}=b_{n-1/2}-h C e_n and e_{n+1}=e_n+h Me^-1 C transpose Mb b_{n+1/2}. Let K=Mb^(1/2) C Me^(-1/2) and h ||K||2<2. The algorithm terminates after N iterations and preserves E_h=1/2[||x_n||2+||y_{n-1/2}||2-h y_{n-1/2} transpose K x_n], where x=Me^(1/2)e,y=Mb^(1/2)b. For h||K||>2 an expanding singular mode exists; equality at 2 may be defective and is excluded.
For Me=Mb=C=[1],S=j=0, forward Euler multiplies W by 1+h2 at every nonzero step.
For the one-mode leapfrog system with K=1,h=2 the update has repeated eigenvalue -1 and a nonzero Jordan nilpotent part, hence generic iterates grow linearly.

On a finite matching tetrahedral mesh choose relative edge space Vh=N_h1 intersect H0(curl), and magnetic face space Wh containing curl Vh. Use edge circulations and oriented face fluxes, incidence curl C and divergence D. For bounded uniformly positive symmetric epsilon,mu assemble Me_ij=integral epsilon phi_i dot phi_j, Mb_ij=integral mu^-1 psi_i dot psi_j; e describes E_h and b describes B_h. Here alpha=min(lambda_min(mu^-1),s2 lambda_min(epsilon)) and M=max(lambda_max(mu^-1),s2 lambda_max(epsilon)).

For the full lowest-order mesh complex discrete harmonic one- and two-mode dimensions equal the corresponding real Betti numbers. For a PEC relative complex, impose its actual relative cohomology or quotient the complete curl kernel; removing only scalar gradients need not remove every zero mode.
